exposure: Mode of hysterectomy (Total Abdominal Hysterectomy vs. Vaginal Hysterectomy)
cohort: The study included 42 patients who underwent caesarean sections (aged 19-37 years) and 140 patients who underwent hysterectomies (aged 40-80 years) at PIMS Hospital between January and December 2024.
finding: The overall incidence of SSI was 22.6% within a 30-day postoperative observation period, with specific risk factors identified for both caesarean sections (maternal age extremes, obesity, GDM, high parity, emergency cases, prolonged labor) and hysterectomies (obesity, excessive blood loss, preoperative anemia or diabetes).
mod_finding: SSIs were more frequent in emergency caesarean cases, but the mode of hysterectomy (TAH vs. VH) did not show a significant difference in SSI rates.
